summary: Writes four pixel/vertex data words (a4/a5/a6/a7) into a texture buffer at a computed slot. Gated on the format identifier at this+0x4C being 1 and the signed flag byte at this+0x20 being negative (bit 7 set). When that flag demands it, allocates/resizes the texture with TextureAllocationWithFormatSizeFlags(this, 0). Reads the row-data pointer through the descriptor at this+0x50 (v9 = descriptor[8]), and if non-null computes the pixel slot as (a2<<7) indexing a 128-byte-stride table reached via this+0x34, scaled by this+0x24, plus a3, shifted <<6 for 64-byte entries; writes components at slot+0, +4, +8 and +0x18. Returns (char)v8, a register-reuse artifact.

local_names.a2: index into a 128-byte-stride table held through the field at this+0x34
local_names.a3: row/offset term added before the 64-byte pixel stride is applied
local_names.a4: pixel/vertex data component written at slot+0
local_names.a5: pixel/vertex data component written at slot+4
local_names.a6: pixel/vertex data component written at slot+8
local_names.a7: pixel/vertex data component written at slot+0x18
local_names.v8: scratch register; carries the flag byte for the bit-7 check and later the descriptor pointer

operations.description: Format gate: the whole body executes only when the format identifier at this+0x4C equals 1
Allocation/overflow flag: when the signed byte at this+0x20 is negative (bit 7 set) the texture is (re)allocated and the write proceeds
TextureAllocationWithFormatSizeFlags(this, 0) allocates or resizes the texture buffer when the flag demands it
Read the texture descriptor pointer at this+0x50, then the row-data pointer v9 = descriptor[8] (descriptor+0x20)
Row-data guard: the write target is computed and written only while v9 is non-null
Compute the pixel slot: (a2<<7) indexes a 128-byte-stride table reached through the field at this+0x34, scaled by this+0x24, offset by a3, then shifted <<6 for 64-byte pixel entries
Write a4 into the pixel entry component at slot+0
Write a5 into the pixel entry component at slot+4
Write a6 into the pixel entry component at slot+8
Write a7 into the pixel entry component at slot+0x18
Returns (char)v8, a decompiler artifact of v8's low byte used as a scratch register; not a meaningful boolean
Invoked on the frame path by particle/render helpers ParticleEffectBillboardQuadSetup, F_3DBoundingBoxRender and WheelContactParticle

clean_pseudocode: dst[0] = a4; dst[1] = a5; dst[2] = a6; dst[6] = a7;
unresolved: The packet labels the four written components on base *(this+0x50) at offsets 0x0/0x4/0x8/0x18, while the raw source writes through the indirection v9 = descriptor[8] plus a computed offset; whether the pixel components live in the descriptor itself or in the row-data buffer is not resolvable from this packet alone
Semantics of a2 (128-byte-stride index) and a3 (row/offset) are DERIVED from the arithmetic, not documented
The meaning of bit 7 of the byte at this+0x20 (needs-allocation vs overflow-ready) is inferred
